newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline Beecham 1996 profits up sharply.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline Beecham 1996 profits up sharply.

text.p: Anglo-U.S. drugs group SmithKline Beecham plc unveiled a sharp rise in profits on Tuesday, although a strong pound hit the group's performance in the fourth quarter.

Pre-tax profit jumped 14 percent to 1.545 billion stg from 1.36 billion in 1995, at the bottom end of analysts' forecasts, while the full-year dividend climbed 25 percent to 17.85 pence from 14.30 pence.

SmithKline Beecham said sales of its newest products again lead the way, rising 37 percent year-on-year. Overall drug sales and operating profit were both up 14 percent, while profit margins stood at 24.8 percent.

Antibiotic Augmentin and fast-growing anti-depressent Paxil/Seroxat were the biggest selling products, both helped by new formulations and indications. Sales of Augmentin rose 4 percent to 868 million pounds, while Paxil, which competes with Eli Lilly & Co's Prozac rose 42 percent to 706 million pounds.

The company said the number of lives covered by its U.S. pharmacy benefit manager climbed 27 percent to 33 million, while the troubled Clinical Laboratories operations staged a modest recovery, with operating profit up seven percent.
Sales at consumer healthcare rose 17 percent while operating profit rose 12 percent.
The company said the strong pound reduced fourth-quarter pre-tax profit by 35 million pounds, and the full-year figure by around 29 million pounds.
